title: HubSpot Seats and Credits Pricing in EMEA | IT SalesaaS
text:
November 10, 2026 · HubSpot

# HubSpot expands its seats and credits pricing pilot to all new customers in EMEA

HubSpot told investors on 4 November 2026 that its pricing pilot now covers all new customers in EMEA. The model drops separate hubs, sells one go-to-market seat and puts AI agents and other usage on a single credit balance. Existing customers stay outside it for now, and no date is set for the rest of the world.

## Key facts

Announced
: 4 November 2026, on the Q3 earnings call
Company
: HubSpot
What changed
: The pricing pilot was extended in Q4 to all new customers in EMEA
New model
: One GTM seat replaces separate hubs; usage runs on HubSpot Credits
Listed prices
: GTM seats from €20 (Starter), €100 (Professional) and €175 (Enterprise) per seat per month
Existing customers and other regions
: No date stated in the announcement

## What HubSpot announced

On its third quarter earnings call on 4 November, HubSpot CEO Yamini Rangan said the company is moving to a hybrid of seats and credits. The pilot began for new customers in the Nordics in April and in Benelux in June. In the fourth quarter it was extended to all new EMEA customers.

The pilot changes three things. A go-to-market seat gives access to all HubSpot capabilities, so buyers no longer purchase separate hubs. The price jump from Starter to Pro gets smaller across the Marketing, Content and Data Hubs. All usage-based features draw on one credit balance.

HubSpot's catalog supplement for this program, as read on 10 November, lists GTM seats from €20 per seat per month on Starter (10 paid seats at most), €100 on Professional and €175 on Enterprise. Included credits are 5,000, 10,000 or 15,000 a month, and unused credits do not roll over. Extra credits cost €0.010 each.

HubSpot says credit usage in the pilot regions is two to three times higher than elsewhere, with more Pro+ customers and a lower average selling price. These are company figures. Which countries count as EMEA and when existing customers might move are not stated in the announcement. HubSpot said it will share more in February.

...

For a sales leader, AI becomes a usage cost that has to be forecast. The supplement prices a Prospecting Agent outreach recommendation at 100 credits per lead, which is €1 at the extra credit rate. The 10,000 credits included with Professional would cover 100 such leads, while one-to-one emails from a connected inbox use none.

...

US buyers have no date, and terms may change before a wider rollout.

title: HubSpot Product and Pricing Changes | HeadsUp
text:
328 changes since July 2025. The most recent was Nov 13, 2026.

Nov 13, 2026

## HubSpot rebrands as "The Customer Relationship Harness"

What changed

- The main headline changed from "Build demand, win deals, and delight customers" to "HubSpot: The Customer Relationship Harness."
- The sub-headline was rewritten to emphasize that while AI knows the world, HubSpot knows "your world" (your specific business data).
- The phrase "HubSpot Agentic Customer Platform" was replaced with "The New Way to Grow."
- The new copy highlights that AI can now "get work done" across different tools, not just inside HubSpot.

Why it matters

HubSpot is shifting its messaging from being a simple "platform" to a "harness" that connects general AI with specific business data. This suggests they are positioning their proprietary data as the essential ingredient that makes AI actually useful for companies.

Nov 11, 2026

## HubSpot launches credit-based pricing for AI

- Introduced a new "HubSpot Credits" system where credits are used when AI features take action.
- Added specific credit allotments to plans: 500 for Starter, 3,000 for Professional, and 5,000 for Enterprise.
- Updated the Sales Hub pricing page to highlight "Deal journey analytics" and "Deal Progression" features.
- Changed the primary navigation links to point directly to pricing pages rather than product overviews.
- Added a promotional bundle offering Revenue Hub at a discount when purchased with Sales Hub.

Why it matters

HubSpot is shifting how it charges for AI features. Instead of just flat monthly fees, they are introducing "HubSpot Credits." This means users pay based on how much work the AI agents actually do, which could change how customers budget for automation.

Nov 10, 2026

## HubSpot Sales Hub adds Agent Builder to plans HubSpot launches dedicated Free Meeting Scheduler

- Added "Agent Builder" to Starter, Professional, and Enterprise plans for Sales Hub.
- Starter users can now build custom agents with simple automation.
- Professional and Enterprise users get advanced agents with event-based triggers.
- Updated the pricing table to show specific limits for features like calling minutes, email templates (up to 10,000), and sales pipelines (up to 350).
- Added new integration mentions for Microsoft Teams, Amplitude, and Adobe Express.
- Removed several promotional banners for "Revenue Hub" and "Small Business Bundles" from the main sales pricing view.
- Replaced the general "Customer Platform" homepage content with a dedicated page for the Free Meeting Scheduler.
- Added specific features for the scheduler, including round-robin booking, group links, and AI-powered meeting prep.
- Updated navigation links to point directly to the meeting scheduler tool instead of general product pages.
- Added a "Related Resources" section with guides on automating meeting follow-ups and setting up team links.
- Included a new FAQ section specifically addressing meeting scheduling software.

Why it matters

HubSpot is moving away from simple tools toward an "agentic" platform. By adding the Agent Builder to paid tiers, they are letting users create their own custom AI bots to handle sales tasks, which could make their software much harder for customers to leave.

HubSpot is shifting focus from a general platform overview to a specific, high-intent tool. By highlighting the meeting scheduler, they are targeting a common pain point to capture leads who might otherwise use standalone tools like Calendly.

title: HubSpot Fall 2026 Spotlight: Breeze Assistant, Smart CRM & Context Home
text:
10.11.2026 

# HubSpot Launches Fall 2026 Spotlight, Headlined by Breeze Assistant, Smart CRM, and Context Home

HubSpot kicked off its Fall 2026 Spotlight in September 2026 and calls it its most significant product release in years. Everything in it runs on what HubSpot calls Growth Context: the business, team, and customer data that makes AI output useful. The headliners are an all-new Breeze Assistant, a self-updating Smart CRM, and Context Home.

## What’s at the Core of the Release?

- Breeze Assistant. It acts on your instructions, assigns specialized AI agents, and produces proposals, reports, and campaign plans grounded in CRM context.
- Smart CRM. The CRM now captures and syncs calls, emails, and meetings on its own, with no manual data entry.
- Context Home. A score shows how complete your context foundation is and where the gaps are.

## What Changes for Marketing and Sales Teams?

- Marketing Studio surfaces insights like AEO visibility scores, underperforming campaign segments, and leads nobody followed up on. Breeze Assistant then plans campaigns, creates content, and personalizes nurture sequences with content and campaign agents.
- ChatGPT Ads integration sends traffic to HubSpot landing pages, enrolls leads in workflows, and attributes them next to other channels. HubSpot says it’s the first CRM to integrate with ChatGPT Ads.
- Microsoft Advertising tracks which ads drive pipeline and revenue and reaches audiences like verified LinkedIn accounts across Bing, Copilot, MSN, Outlook, and other Microsoft surfaces.
- Prospecting Agent now monitors 40+ buying signals, assembles buying groups, and drafts personalized outreach.
- Mobile Notetaker captures meetings in real time, on a call or in person.
- Deal Progression turns meeting transcripts into CRM updates, drafts follow-ups, and keeps deal plans current with one-click approval.
- Revenue Hub generates quotes from full deal context and keeps revenue moving after the deal is signed.

...

- Less CRM admin for reps. Smart CRM, Mobile Notetaker, and Deal Progression turn calls, emails, and meetings into record updates, so reps approve changes instead of typing them in.
- A clear starting point for AI. Context Home puts a score on your data, so you can see which gaps to close first.
- AI ad channels in your pipeline reports. ChatGPT Ads and Microsoft Advertising results land in HubSpot, so you can compare them side by side with the rest of your channels.
- Some features are still in testing. As of September 2026, Marketing Studio, the ChatGPT Ads integration, Mobile Notetaker, and Deal Progression are in public beta, so check which ones your account can use before you plan around them.

title: CRM Pricing in the Age of AI: Salesforce vs. HubSpot
text:
HubSpot is heading in a different direction. It charges for its own agents when they deliver a defined result, keeps its MCP connection free, and is piloting a simpler seats-plus-credits model with new customers in Europe. Both are reasonable answers to the same problem, and both will be harder to budget for than a seat.

...

HubSpot has framed the same shift differently. CEO Yamini Rangan's rule, set out at HubSpot's September Analyst Day, is that AI which helps a person work more effectively belongs in the seat, while AI that does work beyond the people using the software belongs in credits. Her shorter version is that "the quantity goes down only when the value goes up", as Steven Forth's analysis of HubSpot's pricing records it. HubSpot's paid seats have grown about 80% since its 2024 pricing change, to more than 2.5 million, so it's adding a second meter rather than defending the first.

...

## HubSpot: pay when the work gets done

HubSpot opened UNBOUND in September by declaring the Outcomes Era: the idea that AI should be judged on the business results it produces, given the right data and context, and paired with human judgement. Rangan summed up the shift in HubSpot's Q3 results as a move "from tools that help people do work to agents that do the work".

The pricing had already started moving. Since 14 April 2026, Breeze Customer Agent costs $0.50 per resolved conversation, down from $1 per conversation, and Breeze Prospecting Agent costs $1 per lead recommended for outreach. If the visitor ends up asking for a person instead, there's no charge. HubSpot's own line is that "AI should be measured in outcomes, not output" (HubSpot).

Everything settles in HubSpot Credits, priced at one cent each. Starter, Professional and Enterprise include 500, 5,000 and 10,000 credits a month, and admins can set limits by account, feature, action and agent. The overseas pilot sits on top of this: new customers in the Nordics and Benelux get a simplified model of seats plus credits, with spend that can shift between the two, and HubSpot is extending it to new customers across EMEA this quarter.

The contrast with Salesforce is sharpest on MCP. HubSpot's MCP server and its Claude and ChatGPT connectors carry no separate charge on any plan, so a team can point Claude at its HubSpot data today without a second meter running.

There are caveats worth knowing:

- HubSpot defines what counts as an outcome. A conversation counts as resolved unless the visitor asks for a human within 72 hours, and a lead the agent marks as not qualified still counts.
- Credits reset monthly and don't roll over.
- Rangan has said HubSpot will eventually meter and charge for other platforms that rely on its customer data, so free MCP access may not stay free forever.

### Pricing Innovation: Testing the Credit-Based Monetization Model

To address this, the company is currently piloting a radical new pricing structure in the EMEA region, specifically in the Nordics and Benelux markets. This hybrid model moves away from selling individual Hubs and instead offers a unified “go-to-market seat” governed by a system of credits. Early data from the EMEA pilot suggests that this model is driving significantly higher engagement, with credit consumption levels two to three times higher than usage in non-pilot regions. title: HubSpot Agent Hub: What the Agents Do and Where Humans Stay
text:
## What Agent Hub is

On 23 July 2026, HubSpot moved its Breeze Agents into a new home called Agent Hub, and renamed Breeze Studio to Agent Builder. Both are in public beta for Professional and Enterprise plans. Breeze Assistant kept its name.

Agent Hub gives you one view of every agent running across marketing, sales and service: what is active, what it is doing and what it produced, according to Integrate IQ’s write-up of the Fall Spotlight. HubSpot says it does not need a separate licence.

The line-up is the Customer Agent, the Prospecting Agent and the Data Agent, plus three new marketing agents and a Revenue Agent in public beta. Demand Gen Playbook reports that the Prospecting Agent now watches more than 40 buying signals.

## What it costs

Agents run on credits, and credits cost $0.01 each beyond your monthly allowance, according to HubSpot’s pricing page. That page lists 3,000 included credits on Professional and 5,000 on Enterprise. Some sources, including Eesel’s pricing breakdown, put the per-action costs at 100 credits for a Prospecting Agent recommendation on one lead, 50 for a Customer Agent resolved conversation, 10 for a Data Agent prompt about one record and 1,000 for a piece of content from the beta Content Agent. At a cent a credit, that is about $1 a lead and 50 cents a resolution, which matches the pay-per-result prices CMSWire reported for April. Some sources add that agents which were free during the beta now consume credits.

On 15 October, HubSpot announced spend caps, seat-to-credit swaps and flex payment options for exactly this reason: AI usage is growing and customers wanted a ceiling. Set the cap before you switch the agent on, not after the first bill.

title: HubSpot Pricing (2026): Free, Starter & Professional Costs
text:
HubSpot is free to start, but its paid plans range from about $20 per seat to thousands of dollars a month, and the Professional plans add one-time onboarding fees. Here is what each plan costs, what changes when you upgrade, and what a small business will really pay in year one.

Prices last checked November 11, 2026. Prices below were checked on HubSpot’s free and Starter, Sales Hub and Marketing Hub pricing pages on this date. We re-check the prices in every guide at least once a month. By Bradford Gilliland · How we research

## HubSpot pricing at a glance

| Plan | Price | Billing | Who it’s for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0 | Free for up to 2 users | Solo owners and tiny teams getting organized |
| Starter (Customer Platform) | $20/seat/mo list price | Monthly or yearly | Small teams that want marketing, sales and service basics in one place |
| Sales Hub Professional | $90/seat/mo billed yearly, $100 billed monthly | Annual commitment | Sales teams that need more advanced sales tools and automation |
| Marketing Hub Professional | $800/mo billed yearly, $890 billed monthly (3 seats included) | Annual commitment | Businesses running marketing automation at scale |
| Enterprise | Sales Hub from $150/seat/mo; Marketing Hub from $3,600/mo | Yearly, through sales | Larger companies |

New-customer Starter offer: when we checked, HubSpot was advertising “save up to 65% on Starter”: $7 per seat per month billed yearly or $10 billed monthly, down from the $20 list price. It’s for new customers only and HubSpot says select offers are available for a limited time, so check the price and how long it lasts at checkout.

...

### Starter Customer Platform: $20 per seat per month (list)

- Marketing, Sales, Service, Content and Data Hub Starter in one bundle
- 1,000 marketing contacts and 500 HubSpot Credits
- HubSpot branding removed from email, chat, forms and meeting links
- Email marketing up to 5 times your contact tier each month
- Simple sales automation (up to 50 workflows with restricted triggers), up to 15 pipelines
- 500 calling minutes and 1 HubSpot phone number (not in every country)

### Sales Hub Professional: $90 per seat per month (billed yearly)

- Everything in Sales Hub Starter, plus Deal Progression (beta) and more advanced sales tools
- 3,000 HubSpot Credits
- $100 per seat per month if billed monthly, still on an annual commitment
- A required one-time Professional onboarding fee of $1,500

### Marketing Hub Professional: $800 per month (billed yearly)

- Includes 3 core seats; more start at $45 per month each
- 2,000 marketing contacts and 3,000 HubSpot Credits
- Marketing Studio and AEO tools (both in beta) and nurture journeys
- $890 per month if billed monthly, on an annual commitment
- A required one-time Professional onboarding fee of $3,000

title: Latest Updates from HubSpot | From the team at Geear
text:
#### November 11, 2026

Product Update (Now Live) — Schedule-based Workflows, No Data Hub Required

Ever wanted a workflow to run every Monday morning or on the 1st of the month, then hit the Data Hub paywall? Not anymore! Daily, weekly, and monthly scheduled triggers used to need Data Hub, and now any portal with workflows can use them. That makes things like monthly member check-ins, weekly data cleanup, and recurring internal reminders much easier to set up for clients who don’t have Data Hub.

#### September 11, 2026

* Product Update (Public Beta) — Personalized Navigation

Ever watched a new user scroll through 80+ nav items looking for the one tool they actually need? HubSpot's left-hand navigation now adjusts to each user, putting their most-used tools and bookmarks up front. Users can also make it their own: pin or unpin items, create custom groupings, and rearrange everything to match how they work. Watch the quick overview.

What's the impact?

With less clutter, new users get up to speed faster and everyone spends less time hunting for tools. A loan officer or member service rep sees the tools they use every day instead of all 80+. To get started, an admin opts into the beta first, then turns it on for the whole account so each user can join from their own navigation. New users get a navigation built around the use case they pick at signup.

Coming soon: If you'd rather set up navigation for your team ... It will let admins build navigation templates, choose which tools users and teams see, and apply custom groupings.

#### September 1, 2026

Product Update (Public Beta) — Customizable Title Card on CRM Records

...

#### August 5, 2026

Product Update (Now Live) — Transactional SMS

You can now send transactional SMS straight from HubSpot — the time-sensitive, non-marketing texts like appointment confirmations, account alerts, and one-time passcodes. It's a new Transactional SMS Long Code Add-On ($75/month) available on Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise, and it includes setup and maintenance of a dedicated transactional 10DLC number plus registration and 1,000 message segments per month.

What's the impact?

This opens up compliant, real-time texting for our CU clients — think fraud alerts, payment reminders, and OTPs delivered right alongside the automations they already run in HubSpot. A few things worth flagging to clients up front: it's US-based sending to US/Canada (+1) numbers only, the 1,000 segments/month don't roll over, both incoming and outgoing messages count against that limit, and incoming MMS counts as 5 segments each. Handy for scoping which use cases fit inside the base allotment before anyone turns it on. Sent using @U0BFS7JCUGH
